meta.hardware: p6-b300.48xlarge (8x B300 SXM6 275GB, sm_103, NVSwitch, driver 580.159.03)
meta.model: zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (753B MoE/40B active, glm_moe_dsa, MLA+DSA, native MTP)
meta.regime_instrument: engine gauges (token_usage, num_queue_reqs) + nsys --gpu-metrics-device at the knee (DCGM PROF dead on B300/driver-580, see lessons L3)
meta.ttft_measurement_verified: P0 gate closed: bench.py client-side TTFT p95 + sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds (underscore) histogram p95 both non-zero and distinct from E2E before any sweep

configs.description: FP8 floor, TP8, radix cache OFF, no fp8-KV, no spec decode, no HiCache. max-model-len 65536, mem-fraction-static 0.85.
configs.workload: coding-agent (12K cacheable prefix + ~1K suffix, 2048 out, byte-identical shared prefix)
configs.knee: c32 (TTFT p95 12.2s, p99 14.4s — near the 15s ceiling; c64 expected to breach)
configs.regime_note: [gauge-inferred] PREFILL-BOUND. TTFT p95 scales 3.9->6.6->12.2s across c8/16/32 while agg tok/s grows sub-linearly (571->945->1349, ~2.4x for 4x conc). radix OFF => every request re-prefills the 12K shared prefix. num_queue_reqs stayed 0 at c32 (not admission-capped); num_running=18-23. KV pool not saturated. => the binding cost is prefill compute on a repeated prefix, exactly the lever T2 (prefix cache) targets.
configs.notes: Honest FP8 baseline. cache_hit=0 correct (radix disabled). goodput@SLO = 1349 tok/s @ c32.

configs.lever_delta: enable RadixAttention prefix cache (remove --disable-radix-cache). ONLY change vs T0.
configs.description: T0 + prefix cache ON. Tests the regime prediction that the 12K byte-identical prefix is the prefill bottleneck. Expect large TTFT drop + goodput gain at concurrency.
configs.knee: c256 (TTFT p95 10.7s, p99 11.4s, 0 errors — practical SLO ceiling; c512 expected to breach)
configs.delta_vs_parent: +347% goodput at the SLO knee (T0 1348.7@c32 -> T2 6024.8@c256); TTFT p95 12.2s -> 10.7s at far higher load. cache hit 0 -> 0.92.
configs.regime_note: [gauge-inferred] Post-cache the regime is DECODE-BOUND: TTFT now scales ~linearly with conc (1.8/3.2/6.0/10.7s at c32/64/128/256) = batch-decode growth, NOT prefill. Throughput still climbing at c256 (6025 tok/s, no plateau) so not yet compute-saturated; the SLO (TTFT) binds before throughput does. cache hit flat 0.918 across all conc (prefix fully resident).
configs.decision: ACCEPT. New current-best = T2 @ c256, 6025 tok/s. Next lever (single-variable from T2): the regime is decode-bound with throughput still rising, so the candidates are (a) T1 +fp8 KV cache dtype (more KV residency -> higher max batch within SLO; won big on B200 1708->3004) and (b) T3 +MTP/EAGLE spec decode (decode-latency lever). T1 first: it directly extends the decode-bound knee and is the cheapest single change.

configs.lever_delta: add --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3. ONLY change vs T2.
configs.description: T2 + fp8 KV cache. Hypothesis: more KV residency extends the decode-bound knee past c256.

coding_c512.note: SLO BREACH + 28% request failures (1107/1536) — KV/timeout exhaustion at c512

configs.delta_vs_parent: +1.7% @ c256 knee (6024.8 -> 6128.6) — BELOW the 3% plateau threshold.
configs.CORRECTION_2026-06-27: [measured] This lever was effectively a NO-OP, not a weak lever. The T4 pod built WITHOUT --kv-cache-dtype still reports kv_cache_dtype='fp8_e4m3' and allocates KV as torch.float8_e4m3fn (49.2GB) — so fp8 KV is the AUTO-RESOLVED DEFAULT for GLM-5.2 DSA on SGLang v0.5.13 (fp8 model -> fp8 KV). T0 and T2 were ALSO running fp8 KV. Explicitly setting the flag in T1 changed nothing except emitting the 'no scaling factors, defaulting to 1.0' warning. The +1.7% is run-to-run noise. Do NOT credit fp8 KV as a separate lever for this model; it's baked in. (Contrast B200 STAGE6-REPORT 1708->3004 'fp8 KV' gain — re-examine whether that was also default-vs-explicit or a genuine no-cache-regime effect.)
configs.quality_gate: N/A — no-op config, nothing to gate.
configs.regime_note: [measured] fp8 KV is default-on; not a tunable lever here.
configs.decision: REJECT (no-op / within noise). Keep T2 as current-best. PLATEAU STRIKE 1/3. Next lever: T4 TP4+DP2 layout — the B300-unique structural arm (won +19-25% on kimi); single conceptual lever (parallelism layout) from T2.

configs.lever_delta: parallelism layout TP8 -> TP4+DP2 (two 4-GPU replicas). ONLY change vs T2.
configs.description: B300-UNIQUE arm (TP4 = ~188GB/GPU > B200 180GB, fits B300 275GB). The layout that won +19-25% on kimi-k2.6-nvfp4. Tests whether 2 DP replicas beat one TP8 instance for shared-prefix agent traffic.

coding_c384.note: 27% client failures (306/1152) — same class as c512. TTFT p95 9.7s would pass but error rate fails SLO.

coding_c512.note: TTFT p95 13.6s is UNDER SLO, but 32% client-side request failures (489/1536) blow error_rate_max=0.001. server num_retracted=0.

configs.knee: c256 = SLO knee, REPEATABLE/CLEAN: 3 runs 7728/7998 tok/s, 0 errors, TTFT p95 6.66-6.95s. This is the number for fleet sizing. ABOVE c256: c512 breaches TTFT (p95 15.75s > 15s) so it's out regardless. c384 hits ~8900-9390 tok/s (TTFT p95 ~10s, would pass) BUT shows intermittent client-side request failures (0 to 27% across runs) — root-caused to a CLIENT harness artifact (L8: connector limit + chained-process connection reuse + likely ephemeral-port pressure from limit=0 opening ~1152 sockets), NOT a server limit (num_retracted=0 always). c384 is real upside under a production load balancer but NOT banked here — would need an LB-fronted re-test to certify.
configs.knee_measurement_note: [measured, clean] c256 comfortable (7998 tok/s, p95 6.95s). [measured, DISTRIBUTED 2-client certify] c384 = 9900 tok/s, 0/1152 errors, TTFT p95 14.94s (PASSES) but p99 15.51s (marginal edge). The single-client c384 failures were 100% harness artifact — 2 client pods on separate nodes gave zero errors. c320 measuring to pin the comfortable (p95 AND p99 < 15s) knee.

distributed_certification.method: 2 client pods on separate m6i nodes hitting B300 node-IP:30000, concurrency split, simultaneous; aggregated tput over global wall window + merged TTFT percentiles

c320.note: COMFORTABLE KNEE — both p95 and p99 well under 15s with headroom. RECOMMENDED operating point.

c384.note: true ceiling — p95 passes, p99 marginally over 15s

configs.RECOMMENDED_OPERATING_POINT: c320/node: 9271 tok/s, TTFT p95 8.1s, 0 errors. c256 (7998, p95 7s) for extra latency margin; c384 (9900, p95 14.9s) is the hard ceiling.
configs.delta_vs_parent: +28.3% goodput @ c256 knee (T2 6024.8 -> T4 7728.1) AND lower TTFT (10.7s -> 6.66s). Holds SLO-TTFT to c512 where T2 breached. Confirms the kimi +19-25% layout finding, even larger here (+28%).
configs.regime_note: [gauge-inferred] Two TP4 replicas beat one TP8 instance: less per-step TP collective overhead (TP4 NVLink collectives are cheaper than TP8) + 2x scheduler parallelism for the shared-prefix decode-bound regime. Each replica holds the full 12K prefix in its own radix cache (cache hit stays 0.918). This is the B300-unique win — physically impossible on B200.
configs.decision: ACCEPT. New current-best = T4 TP4+DP2, SLO knee c256 ~7998 tok/s (+28-33% vs T2). Resets plateau counter. Next single-variable lever from T4: T3 +NEXTN MTP spec decode (native MTP, num_nextn_predict_layers=1, card claims +20% accept-len) — the remaining high-rank decode lever.
configs.held_out_quality_gate: PASS (run on the WINNING config, reward-hacking guard). 3 frozen coding tasks the config was NOT tuned on: Q1 off-by-one last-index fix = correct (reverse range); Q2 palindrome one-liner = correct (walrus + alnum + [::-1]); Q3 glm47 tool-calling = well-formed tool_call emitted (name+JSON args). T4 goodput is NOT bought with degraded quality.

configs.lever_delta: add --speculative-algorithm NEXTN (native MTP, num-steps 1, draft-tokens 2). PAIRED with --max-running-requests 512 — NOT a 2nd free variable: MTP silently auto-resets max-running to 48 if unset (memory L1), which would cripple the batch and invalidate the comparison; 512 keeps the batch ceiling comparable to T4's effective-unlimited default.
configs.description: T4 + native MTP spec decode. Decode-latency lever. Expect TTFT-neutral, decode-throughput up at low-mid concurrency; spec decode often REGRESSES at high concurrency (draft overhead per the spec's own T3 caveat + single-stream-decode-levers memory).
configs.delta_vs_parent: c8 +6% (683 vs T2 643, but T4 wasn't measured at c8), c64 +1.4% (3149 vs 3106), c256 -12.2% (7021.7 vs T4 7998.1). At the SLO KNEE (c256, the customer operating point) MTP REGRESSES.
configs.regime_note: [measured] MTP accept_length ~1.6 across all concurrency (model card claimed +20% accept-len; real acceptance on this coding/reasoning workload is modest — drafts a useful token ~60% of steps). At low conc the extra accepted token slightly helps; at the c256 knee the per-step draft+verify compute overhead on an already-full batch outweighs the ~1.6 acceptance, costing -12%. Classic spec-decode-regresses-under-load (matches spec T3 caveat + project_single_stream_decode_levers).
configs.decision: REJECT at the knee. MTP is a LATENCY lever for low-concurrency single-stream serving (would help a conc=1-8 latency SLO), but the customer objective is goodput@high-concurrency where it costs -12%. Keep T4 as current-best. PLATEAU STRIKE 2/3. Document MTP as a conditional lever (enable only for low-QPS latency-first deployments).

configs.lever_delta: add --chunked-prefill-size 8192 (SGLang MNBT/max-num-batched-tokens equivalent; default is 16384). ONLY change vs T4.
configs.description: T4 + smaller prefill chunk. B200 STAGE6 found MNBT 8192 beat the 16384 default on TTFT at the SLO knee (smaller chunks interleave decode more -> lower TTFT -> higher SLO-passing concurrency). Re-test on B300 (FRESH NODE ip-10-2-31-98, distributed 2-client driver for clean TTFT).

default_16384_c320_distributed.note: fresh-node clean anchor; matches prior 9271 within noise

configs.delta_vs_parent: c320: -2.6% tok/s (9400->9157), +0.7s TTFT — slightly WORSE at the knee. BUT c384: 10246 tok/s @ TTFT p95 10.06s, clean — vs default-16384 c384 which hit p95 14.94s/p99 15.51s. 8192 gives much better TTFT HEADROOM at c384, extending the comfortable ceiling from c320 to c384.
configs.regime_note: [measured] Opposite of the B200 finding (where 8192 beat default at the knee). Here prefix cache already removed the prefill pressure that MNBT addressed on B200's no-cache long-context tests, so at c320 the smaller chunk just adds scheduling overhead (-2.6%). The win is at HIGHER concurrency: smaller prefill chunks interleave decode better, so c384 stays at p95 10s vs default's 14.9s. Net: 8192 trades a tiny c320 loss for a real c384 gain.
configs.decision: CONDITIONAL ACCEPT. At the c320 recommended knee, default-16384 is marginally better (9400 vs 9157). But 8192 unlocks a comfortable c384 operating point (10246 tok/s, p95 10s) that default-16384 cannot hold (p99 breaches). Best-of-both: default-16384 if targeting c320; 8192 if pushing to c384 for max throughput/node. Testing 4096 next.

configs.description: Smallest prefill chunk tested — extends the 8192 trend.
configs.delta_vs_parent: c320 -5.9% (9400->8842), c384 -2.5% vs 8192. Strictly DOMINATED by 8192 (lower throughput AND higher TTFT at both points).
configs.decision: REJECT. 4096 is dominated by 8192 everywhere. Monotonic trend confirmed: smaller chunk = lower throughput, no TTFT benefit below 8192. MNBT SWEEP COMPLETE.
configs.mnbt_sweep_conclusion: chunked-prefill-size is a modest CEILING-tuning knob, not a major lever, in this prefix-cached decode-bound regime. RECOMMENDATION: default-16384 for the c320 knee (9400 tok/s); 8192 only if pushing per-node load to c384 (10246 tok/s, p95 10s). 4096 never. This is OPPOSITE the B200 STAGE6 finding (8192 won there) because B200's win was in no-prefix-cache long-context prefill pressure that prefix cache eliminates here. PLATEAU: no config beat the T4 c320 baseline at the knee -> STRIKE 3/3 -> loop plateau reached, T4 (default MNBT) remains the winner.

configs.lever_delta: quantization FP8 -> official nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (modelopt NVFP4, shared-expert-preserved recipe). Image lmsysorg/sglang:dev-glm52-nvfp4 (transformers 5.8.1), --quantization modelopt_fp4. Same TP4+DP2 + prefix-cache layout.
configs.description: The big open question from the B200 report: does the OFFICIAL NVFP4 recipe (only MoE-expert linears quantized, shared expert preserved) beat FP8 in this decode-bound regime on B300? B200 community full-quant checkpoint regressed -55-60%; spec flagged official as unverified.
configs.functional_check: PASS — clean correct factorial fn, no quant garbage, finish_reason=stop
configs.delta_vs_parent: c256 -56% (7998->3539), c320 -52% (9400->4550), c384 -53% (10246->4864). NVFP4 is ~HALF the throughput of FP8 at every concurrency.
configs.regime_note: [measured] NOT a kernel fallback — logs confirm NVFP4 uses the SAME flashinfer_trtllm MoE backend as FP8 (ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod on sm100), correct path. The regression is intrinsic to the current NVFP4 MoE kernel: (1) log says 'Detected nvfp4 checkpoint ... format is EXPERIMENTAL and subject to change'; (2) 'FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE deferred finalize is DISABLED' for the NVFP4 quant method (an optimization FP8 keeps); (3) batched-decode is compute-bound on the NVFP4 dequant path. The 2.4x larger KV pool (2.29M vs 956K tokens) does NOT help because the bottleneck is MoE GEMM compute, not KV residency. TTFT non-monotonic (c256 13.4s > c320 8.2s) = kernel inefficiency artifact, not a residency limit.
configs.decision: REJECT decisively. NVFP4 ~halves throughput vs FP8 (-52 to -56%) for this batched serving workload. CONFIRMS+EXTENDS the B200 community-checkpoint finding (-55-60%) to the OFFICIAL shared-expert-preserved recipe on B300 — the open question is now answered: NVFP4 does NOT win here. NVFP4's value remains (a) VRAM-constrained single-node fit (433 vs 707GB) and (b) possibly single-stream c1 latency (untested this run). For the customer's high-concurrency goodput objective, FP8 T4 is the clear winner. Root cause is an experimental/unoptimized NVFP4 MoE kernel (deferred-finalize disabled) — re-test when SGLang NVFP4 support matures past 'experimental'.
